_comment: Métier scam-technique database. Each entry is one recruiter-scam tell matched against the message body. Loaded into the scam_patterns table on startup; the DB also accepts live additions. To add a technique, append an entry and restart (or INSERT directly). polarity: 'risk' raises the scam score, 'trust' lowers it. weight = points (0-100 scale, engine caps the total).

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Legitimate recruiters are paid by the employer. A candidate never pays to apply or get hired.

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Employers cover background-check costs; charging the candidate is a scam tell.

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Paid training before hire is a classic advance-fee scam.

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Placement fees are paid by employers, never candidates.

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Real employers provide equipment; a deposit request is a scam.

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Required paid certifications tied to a job offer are a pay-to-play tell.

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Onboarding/processing fees are never charged to candidates by real employers.

patterns.title: Upfront fee requested
patterns.explanation: Onboarding is an employer cost; charging for it is a scam.

patterns.title: Paid starter kit
patterns.explanation: 'Starter kits' you must buy are a common job-scam mechanic.

patterns.title: Refundable deposit requested
patterns.explanation: 'Refundable' deposits rarely are; no legitimate hire requires one.

patterns.title: Asked to buy equipment
patterns.explanation: Being told to buy your own gear before starting is a scam tell.

patterns.title: Sensitive personal info requested early
patterns.explanation: SSN should never be shared before a signed offer.

patterns.title: Sensitive personal info requested early
patterns.explanation: SSN should never be shared before a signed offer.

patterns.title: Banking details requested early
patterns.explanation: Bank/routing details before hire paperwork is a data-harvesting tell.

patterns.title: Banking details requested early
patterns.explanation: Routing numbers are not needed before employment is confirmed.

patterns.title: Direct-deposit setup before offer
patterns.explanation: Direct deposit is set up after hire, never during outreach.

patterns.title: Government ID requested early
patterns.explanation: Passport/ID before a formal offer is identity harvesting.

patterns.title: Government ID requested early
patterns.explanation: Driver's license before an offer is unnecessary and risky.

patterns.title: DOB requested early
patterns.explanation: Date of birth before hire paperwork is a data-harvesting tell.

patterns.title: Early 'identity verification'
patterns.explanation: Requests to 'verify your identity' with documents just to start are suspicious.

patterns.title: Pressure / urgency tactics
patterns.explanation: Manufactured urgency rushes you past verification — a scam hallmark.

patterns.title: Pressure / urgency tactics
patterns.explanation: Real hiring runs on a defined timeline, not 'respond immediately.'

patterns.title: Pressure / urgency tactics
patterns.explanation: Artificial scarcity is a pressure tactic.

patterns.title: Pressure / urgency tactics
patterns.explanation: Artificial scarcity is a pressure tactic.

patterns.title: Pressure / urgency tactics
patterns.explanation: 'Today only' deadlines are designed to stop you verifying.

patterns.title: Pressure / urgency tactics
patterns.explanation: 'Last chance' framing is a manipulation tactic.

patterns.title: Pushes to an off-channel app
patterns.explanation: Moving to WhatsApp/Telegram early avoids a paper trail — a strong scam tell.

patterns.title: Pushes to an off-channel app
patterns.explanation: Telegram is heavily used by job scammers to evade verification.

patterns.title: Pushes to an off-channel app
patterns.explanation: Pushing to encrypted personal messaging early is suspicious for a recruiter.

patterns.title: Pushes to text/chat only
patterns.explanation: Insisting on text/chat instead of a real call is a common scam pattern.

patterns.pattern: i hope this (message|email) finds you well
patterns.title: Generic AI/template phrasing
patterns.explanation: Boilerplate opener — a yellow flag only; weigh it with other signals, since real recruiters use templates too.

patterns.title: Generic AI/template phrasing
patterns.explanation: Mass-outreach opener with no real personalization — a mild tell.

patterns.title: Unfilled template placeholder
patterns.explanation: Leftover [First Name]/[Company] fields prove an unproofed mass blast.

patterns.title: Ghost-job language
patterns.explanation: 'We'll keep your resume on file' often means there is no real opening.

patterns.title: Vague WFH bait
patterns.explanation: Generic 'work from home opportunity' with no specifics is common scam bait.

patterns.title: No interview / no experience needed
patterns.explanation: Real roles have a process; 'no interview needed' signals a scam.

patterns.title: Guarantee that can't be made
patterns.explanation: No legitimate recruiter guarantees placement or income.

patterns.title: Implausible pay rate
patterns.explanation: Daily/hourly pay well above market for the role is a too-good-to-be-true tell.
